summary: The charter of the Internet Architecture Board, a technical advisory group of the Internet Society. It describes how the IAB is formed and operates. It was replaced by RFC 1601.

plainLanguage.summary: This 1992 document is the charter of the Internet Architecture Board, the group of technical experts that advises the Internet Society and publishes the standards documents. It says what the IAB does, how many members it has and how they are chosen, and how its chair and the heads of its task forces are appointed.

subtitle: The founding rules of the Internet technical advisory board.

tldr.problem: The Internet Architecture Board needed a formal charter defining its membership, governance and responsibilities as a technical advisory group of the Internet Society.
tldr.mechanism: Establish the IAB with up to 15 individual members nominated by the IAB, Internet Society leadership, or member petition. Define the roles of the IAB chair, RFC Editor, IETF chair and IRTF chair, with appointment and removal procedures.
tldr.outcome: The charter formalizes how Internet architecture decisions are made and how the standards and RFC publication process are managed. This version was replaced by RFC 1601.

today: The unit metadata records RFC 1358 as Informational and obsoleted by RFC 1601, which updated the IAB charter.

sections.title: The IAB and Its Role
sections.content:
The Internet Architecture Board (IAB) operates as a technical advisory group of the Internet Society. Its responsibilities include expert oversight of the architecture of the worldwide multiprotocol Internet, editorial management and publication of the RFC series, development and approval of Internet Standards, advice to the Internet Society's Board of Trustees on technical and architectural matters, and representation of the Society in liaison relationships with other organizations.

The IAB may be charged with additional responsibilities by the Internet Society, or take on additional activities as the Society's needs demand.
sections.plainLanguage: The IAB is the group of technical experts who advise on how to build the Internet and who publishes the standards documents. It can be given extra jobs when needed.

sections.title: Membership and Governance
sections.content:
The IAB consists of no more than 15 members, who serve as individuals and not as representatives of any company or agency. Members are nominated by the IAB, the President of the Internet Society, the Board of Trustees, or by a petition of at least 1 percent of the Internet Society membership, or 150 members if the membership exceeds 15,000. The Board of Trustees must approve or disapprove a nomination within 60 days, by a three-fifths vote.

Any member may be replaced by the Board of Trustees with a four-fifths vote, or upon a petition of at least 5 percent of the voting membership. The Board reviews each member's contribution at three-year intervals and explicitly reaffirms or revokes the membership. Members serve as volunteers without compensation, except that the President may approve expense reimbursement and, with Board approval, compensation in cases the Board considers essential.
sections.plainLanguage: The IAB has at most 15 members who are chosen by the board, the Society's leaders, or by members signing a petition. They are volunteers and are reviewed every three years.

sections.title: Officers and Task Forces
sections.content:
The members elect one of their number as chair of the IAB, who may be removed by a two-thirds vote of the members. The chair may organize the IAB as seen fit and, with the approval of at least two-thirds of the membership, appoints an Editor for the RFC series. If the RFC Editor is not an IAB member, the position serves ex officio. The chair also appoints, under the same approval, the chair of the Internet Engineering Task Force and the chair of the Internet Research Task Force, the IAB's initial task forces.

The Internet Society provides secretariat support for the IAB and its groups, subject to Board approval. It also publishes, at least every six months, a definitive record of the status of the Internet Standards process, and the Internet Society News serves as the publication of record for IAB actions.
sections.plainLanguage: The members pick a chair. That chair appoints the RFC Editor and the heads of two task forces, one for engineering and one for research. The Society provides staff support and reports on standards status at least twice a year.
